note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

precepts.text: That I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel; the Most High calls his people, the children of Israel, his armies.
precepts.point: The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order; that is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 17: Not by Sword and Spear

precepts.why:
David asked, “What shall be done to the man that killeth this Philistine, and taketh away the reproach from Israel? for who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God?”

The soldiers themselves did not understand that they were the armies of the living God; David, a sheep keeper sent on an errand, knew it. The Most High said it in Egypt: “that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” He calls his people, the children of Israel, his armies.

Israel is the army of the Most High, and every army requires order. That is why there are captains and officers, and despising that order is despising the army of the living God.

points: That I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments. You think when God delivered us out of Egypt he was just delivering a people? No, God was bringing out an army: an army to judge the nations. That is why he says in the fourth generation he will bring them back into the land, because the sin of the Amorites was not yet full.

The fish that was in the river died; and the river stank, and the Egyptians could not drink of the water of the river; and there was blood throughout all the land of Egypt. That is what happened in ancient Egypt. Now remember what the Lord said: I will smite you with plagues like as before.
The Lord made Moses a god to Pharaoh, and Aaron his brother was his prophet. Moses was as God and Aaron was the mouthpiece, because Moses kept saying he was of uncircumcised lips.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: It was Aaron who cast down the rod before Pharaoh, and it became a serpent. A lot of people to this day say it was Moses with the rod, because they do not read the Bible; Moses was telling Aaron what to do, and it was Aaron's rod that turned into the serpent.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: The magicians of Egypt did in like manner with their enchantments, and their rods became serpents; but Aaron's rod swallowed up their rods.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: All the waters of Egypt were turned to blood, in the streams, the rivers, the ponds, the pools, and in vessels of wood and vessels of stone; the fish died and the river stank.
With this first plague the Most High was mocking Sobek, the Egyptian idol god of the rivers, showing that he could not defend his own waters.

note.label: Exodus 7: Aaron's Rod and the River Turned to Blood

points: The magicians did so with their enchantments, but they could only copy the plague; they could not turn the water back clear. Seven days were fulfilled after the Lord had smitten the river.
